title: Rafael and the Wolf
premise: Odile Quintana has survived seven years in the city of Vellamare by selling charms too small to notice, hiding the gift her dead mistress called a debt. When the crown's witch-hunt turns neighbor against neighbor, Odile learns the truth she fled: her old master Rafael sold her name to the crown years ago, and the hunters are following his map. To escape, she must find the Hollow Door—the last crossing out of a country that erased itself from every map—and the only person who knows its location is Rafael himself, now the hunt's chief architect. In the end, Odile confronts him at the Door, refuses both his bargain and his apology, and steps through alone, carrying the names of everyone who couldn't.
about_author: Theo Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. He writes about magic as bureaucracy and survival as an art form from a coastal town that appears on no tourist maps.

chapters.title: Salt on the Sill
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She sells a luck-charm to a fisherman's widow in Vellamare's gray market, establishing her careful invisibility and small kindnesses. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking constant fear.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Criers announce the Edict of Ash: all gifted persons must register or be hunted. A client she trusts is dragged from his shop. Emotional beat: the safe world cracks open; denial curdles into urgency.

chapters.title: What the Charm Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She burns her stock and finds among it a charm she doesn't remember making—her own handwriting, seven years older, addressed to herself. Emotional beat: uncanny dread; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Neighbors
chapters.summary: POV of Tomas, a dockhand who owes Odile money. He weighs reporting her for the reward against an old debt of gratitude. Emotional beat: ordinary complicity; how hunts are fed by small betrayals.

chapters.title: The Name on the List
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A sympathetic clerk shows her the registry: her true name, entered seven years ago, with a signature she recognizes—Rafael's. Emotional beat: betrayal detonates; the person who taught her sold her.

chapters.title: Running Water
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She flees the city by night along the aqueduct, meeting Brisa, a smuggler girl with a boat and no questions. Emotional beat: fragile alliance; first breath of freedom that tastes like exile.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Brisa's POV. On the river they pass villages renamed, shrines defaced, maps repainted—Vellamare erasing its own magical history. Emotional beat: grief for a culture being unmade in real time.

chapters.title: Hollow Bell
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They shelter with a defrocked bell-keeper, Ivo, who once rang warnings for hedge-witches and now keeps one bell for the dead. He speaks of the Hollow Door. Emotional beat: inherited memory; hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV of Captain Ferro, leading the hunt. We see the machinery of persecution: quotas, informers, and Rafael's annotated maps. Emotional beat: chilling competence; evil as paperwork.

chapters.title: Rafael
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The master witch, now crown advisor, justifies his choices—he registered everyone to save 'the useful ones.' He learns Odile still lives. Emotional beat: self-deception dressed as mercy; corruption wearing a mentor's face.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Ford
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Soldiers corner them at a ford; Brisa is taken buying Odile time to escape upstream. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt; the cost of being the one who runs.

chapters.title: Ash Market
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In a refugee camp she trades charms again, this time openly, and hears stories of others who reached the Door—and what it demanded. Emotional beat: community rebuilt from ash; courage going viral.

chapters.title: Ivo's Map
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She returns to find Ivo dying; he gives her the bell-rope knotted with the Door's location and asks her to ring it once for him. Emotional beat: inheritance; the dead passing the torch.

chapters.title: What the Gift Is
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, interior. Hiding in a cave, she finally examines the old charm to herself and deciphers her mistress's real lesson: the gift grows when used for others, starves when hidden. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed; fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Ferro's Net
chapters.summary: Captain Ferro's POV. Using Rafael's map, he predicts her route and seals the mountain passes. Emotional beat: tightening vise; the hunter's cold satisfaction beginning to sour into obsession.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her only open path leads through Rafael's estate. Disguised as a servant, she walks the halls where she was apprenticed. Emotional beat: haunted homecoming; seeing the teacher's rot up close.

chapters.title: The Library of Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In Rafael's library she finds his ledger—every witch he registered, each entry annotated with their fate. She copies the names of the dead onto her arms. Emotional beat: witness as resistance; rage refined into purpose.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Odile and Rafael, alternating close third. He catches her, offers partnership and protection if she surrender the Door's secret. She refuses. Emotional beat: the moral climax of wills; she stops being his apprentice in speech.

chapters.title: The Hollow Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She reaches the Door—a seam in a cliff face that opens only for those who speak the names of the lost. Ferro arrives with soldiers as she begins the naming. Emotional beat: race against annihilation; ritual under fire.

chapters.title: Ring the Bell
chapters.summary: Multi-POV interleave: Odile naming the dead, Ferro hesitating as the names indict him, Rafael arriving too late to bargain. The Door opens. Emotional beat: climax; memory itself becomes the key and the weapon.

chapters.title: One Set of Footprints
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Offered a last chance to bring Rafael through, she leaves him on the wrong side with his ledger burning. She steps through alone. Emotional beat: severance; freedom purchased with loneliness.

chapters.title: The Other Shore
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Beyond the Door, in a country that remembers magic, she plants Ivo's bell-rope and begins teaching—starting with the names written on her skin. Emotional beat: resolution; survival transformed into stewardship.
